title: Investigating the Relationship Between Measures of the Hearing Nerve and Speech Perception Outcomes in Adult Nexa Cochlear Implant Recipients
official: Prospective, Interventional, Multicentre Feasibility Investigation Evaluating Objective Measures and Clinical Outcomes in Adult Nexa® Cochlear Implant Recipients
summary:
This study aims to learn more about the information that can be obtained directly from measurements through a Nexa cochlear implant during and after surgery. Researchers will investigate whether these measurements can help understand how the implant is interacting with the inner ear and hearing nerve, where the electrodes are positioned inside the cochlea, and potentially how the implant should be programmed and how well a person detects sounds.

The study will also evaluate how well two methods agree in determining the position of the electrode contacts relative to the anatomy of the inner ear and the hearing nerve. One method uses measurements after surgery made through the implant itself. The other uses medical Computed Tomography(CT) imaging made after the surgery. The information collected will also contribute to a clinical research database that may be used to support future research and development. Participants will be told about this potential future use when they provide consent.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Aged 18 years or older (no upper age limit).
2. Candidate for CI1032 cochlear implantation as per the local sensorineural hearing loss criteria.
3. Sufficient proficiency in the language used to conduct the study procedures, as determined by the investigator.
4. Availability of pre-op CT scan of the cochlear region meeting quality requirements as determined by the sponsor.
5. Willing and able to provide written informed consent and to comply with all requirements of the protocol.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Previous cochlear implantation in the same ear.
2. Cochlear implant in the contralateral ear.
3. Have an unaided air conduction pure tone average (average of unaided thresholds at 0.5, 1, 2 and 4 kHz) ≤40 dB HL in the contralateral ear measured within the last 12 months
4. Severe or greater sensorineural hearing loss prior to 2 years of age, as documented in medical history.
5. Deafness due to lesions of the auditory nerve or central auditory pathway.
6. Cochlear ossification or anatomical anomaly precluding full electrode array insertion.
7. Diagnosis of auditory neuropathy.
8. Additional conditions preventing or restricting participation in the audiological evaluations, as determined by the investigator.
9. Pregnant or breastfeeding women.
10. Unrealistic expectations on the part of the subject regarding the potential benefits, risks, and limitations of the surgical procedure and device.
11. Unable or unwilling to comply with the requirements of the clinical investigation as determined by the Investigator.
12. Investigator site personnel directly affiliated with this study and/or their immediate families; immediate family is defined as a spouse, parent, child, or sibling.
13. Cochlear employees or employees of Contract Research Organisations or contractors engaged by Cochlear for the purposes of this investigation.
14. Current participation, or participation in another interventional clinical study/trial in the past 30 days, involving an investigational drug or device (unless determined by the Sponsor to not impact this investigation).
